summary.intent: Fix a Web3Auth network mismatch error in production builds by aligning the network configuration with the actual client ID registration on sapphire_devnet.
summary.outcome: PR #461 was created on FSM1/cipher-box with the desktop Core Kit fix. The web app core-kit.ts change was subsequently reverted after the user clarified it was unnecessary, since staging already works correctly there.

repo: Web3Auth client ID is registered on sapphire_devnet, not mainnet — production builds were incorrectly mapped to MAINNET causing network mismatch on login.
The repo has separate Web3Auth core-kit configs for web (apps/web/src/lib/web3auth/core-kit.ts) and desktop; the fix only needed to apply to the desktop config.
VITE_ENVIRONMENT=production is set for production builds, which feeds into the WEB3AUTH_NETWORK mapping logic.
The staging environment config was already correct and did not need changes.

code.finding: This file was incorrectly modified and then reverted — the web app's network config did not need to change; only the desktop Core Kit config required the production→DEVNET mapping fix.

workflow: GITHUB_TOKEN env var can interfere with gh CLI authentication; unsetting it with `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN` resolved the auth issue without requiring a full gh auth login.
gh CLI was not authenticated in the shell environment, requiring a workaround to create the PR.

friction: gh CLI was unauthenticated, blocking PR creation and requiring the user to supply a workaround (`env -u GITHUB_TOKEN`).
The web core-kit.ts was modified unnecessarily and had to be reverted, adding an extra commit to the PR.
open_items: Verify that production desktop builds and web deploys initialize Web3Auth without network mismatch errors after the fix.
Confirm login flows (Google, Email, Wallet) work end-to-end in production builds.
Consider documenting that the Web3Auth client ID is on sapphire_devnet to prevent future misconfiguration.
